A chat with a General Counsel of any respectable multinational will disclose a disquiet about the increasing costs, delays and unpredictability normally associated with arbitration in India. Thus, the real question to address is why the system, as it currently stands, is not consistently delivering on its promise within the Indian context. Recent remarks have brought this debate into sharp focus. On the one hand, there are concerns that aspects of the current arbitral framework may be undermining its effectiveness. On the other, there is a strong and concurrent recognition of the tremendous scope of arbitration and mediation in the light of mounting pendency before courts . This apparent paradox is significant. It reflects not a system in decline, but one at a crossroads: simultaneously critiqued for its shortcomings while at the same time seen as an essential solution to endemic judicial burdens. items.title: Supreme Court issues advisory against fake websites impersonating its official portal
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday warned the public against fraudulent websites impersonating its official online portal. In a public notice, the Supreme Court registry specifically highlighted one website sp-court-in.com which is currently impersonating the official website of the top court. The said the website may deceive people through phishing mechanisms and could be used to obtain sensitive personal information and confidential credentials, the notice warned. "Cybercriminals through the aforementioned link may attempt to solicit sensitive personal data and confidential credentials of the public. All stakeholders are strictly cautioned against divulging any personal / financial information, as such disclosures may facilitate the theft of data by these perpetrators," cautioned the Registry. The advisory was issued in continuation of earlier public notices dated July 16, 2025 and April 28, 2026 , warning about fake websites designed to clone the Supreme Court's official website. The registry urged people to remain vigilant and verify the authenticity of electronic communications before engaging with them. items.title: Vishwanath & Sons: Suriya, Mamitha & Radhika shine in this wholesome family entertainer
items.summary: After the loud and action-heavy Karuppu , which marked Suriya’s comeback this year, Vishwanath & Sons sees the actor in a completely different space. Written and directed by Venky Atluri, the film is a warm, feel-good family entertainer that derives much of its charm from its characters, relationships, and its belief in the possibility of healing. The film follows 40-year-old Sanjay Vishwanath (Suriya), an Olympic gold medallist and successful businessman who appears to have everything one could want. He is wealthy, admired, and one of the country’s most eligible bachelors. Yet he has decided never to marry, a choice rooted in a childhood trauma that continues to shape his relationships. His decision deeply upsets his mother Nirmala Devi (Radhika Sarathkumar), who wants him to marry and continue the family lineage. When she falls ill, Sanjay decides to partly fulfil her wish by having a baby through surrogacy. But the child develops a life-threatening condition and requires a bone marrow transplant.
